facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and conflicts
facts.text: - Going concern. Q2-26 10-Q page:11: "raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern", and "management’s plans do not alleviate substantial doubt". The Q1-26 10-Q and the 10-K do not carry this language. The evidence is a change between filings, not a conflict; downstream modules must date it to the June 30, 2026 report. - Covenant description. The waiver is called a waiver of the "consolidated net leverage ratio covenant" at Q2-26 10-Q page:11 and page:38, while the covenant description at page:37 is a "maximum first lien net leverage ratio" tested when utilization exceeds 25% of commitments. The same page:38 later refers to the "consolidated first lien net leverage ratio covenant". The 10-K threshold was 30% (page:165 "exceed 30% of"). The wording difference is unresolved without the Credit Agreement and waiver, and CP-2 must carry it as a gap, not choose a definition. - Revolver capacity. Q2-26 10-Q page:33: "there was $195.8 million available under the Company’s Revolving Credit Facility" and availability "will be further reduced to approximately $319 million" from October 2026. The same page states a total reduced commitment of about $519.3 million in February 2026. The balance sheet debt table shows Revolving Credit Facility 303,750 outstanding at page:31. Any liquidity consumer must keep these separate and must not infer letters of credit. - Carrying amount versus principal. Page:31 "Long-term debt, including current portion 4,506,700 4,500,657" is after discount and a fair value adjustment, while page:37 maturities total "$ 4,910,068". The two are different bases, not a conflict; the note footnote (3) at page:32 explains the fair value adjustment. - 10-K internal wording. The risk factor summary at page:20 refers to "material weaknesses" while the body at page:51 describes "a material weakness". The count is unresolved from text; the adverse internal control opinion at page:102 is unambiguous. - Preliminary release versus 10-K. The Q4-25 release is labelled preliminary and announces an extension for the 10-K, which was signed March 23, 2026. Revenue of $2,436,189 thousand for the Successor period in the release (page:2 "Total $ 746,245 $ 580,365 $ 2,436,189 $ 220,498 $ 2,450,478") matches the 10-K MD&A summary of $2,436.2 million (page:75). No conflict found on revenue; other release figures must be checked against the 10-K before use.

Page:31 "Long-term debt, including current portion 4,506,700 4,500,657" is after discount and a fair value adjustment, while page:37 maturities total "$ 4,910,068". The two are different bases, not a conflict; the note footnote (3) at page:32 explains the fair value adjustment.

- Preliminary release versus 10-K. The Q4-25 release is labelled preliminary and announces an extension for the 10-K, which was signed March 23, 2026. Revenue of $2,436,189 thousand for the Successor period in the release (page:2 "Total $ 746,245 $ 580,365 $ 2,436,189 $ 220,498 $ 2,450,478") matches the 10-K MD&A summary of $2,436.2 million (page:75). facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported financial base is usable for leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity analysis, with firm limits. Debt, cash, maturities, cash paid for interest, Adjusted EBITDA and its reconciliation are all printed in filed documents, so the ratios below are calculated only from printed figures. The ratios are not like-for-like across dates. Reported 2025 amounts are split at the February 7, 2025 merger, so each last-twelve-month figure is a sum of a Predecessor stub and Successor periods. The Intralot group debt entered the balance sheet in the fourth quarter of 2025 and is counted in full at each later date, while the Intralot B2B earnings count only from October 8, 2025, so leverage at the later dates is higher than a pro forma view would show; the sources do not provide that view. Adjusted EBITDA is after cash rent on triple net operating leases, so operating lease liabilities are excluded from debt for consistency, and are shown separately. The June 30, 2026 liquidity position and the unfinished financing plans described in the going concern note are the main credit issue; the ratios describe the burden, not the headroom under any covenant, because the covenant definitions are not supplied.

facts.label: Liquidity and covenant facts
facts.text: - Revolver: commitments were reduced to about 519.3 million in February 2026; from October 2026 total availability falls to about 319 million; 195.8 million was available at June 30, 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:33). Commitments less borrowings is 215.55 million, so 19.75 million of commitments is neither drawn nor reported as available; the filing does not say why, and letters of credit are not named. - Financial covenant: when utilization exceeds 25% of commitments, the revolver requires "a first lien secured net indebtedness to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of 4.00 to 1.00" (Q2-26 10-Q page:65). Utilization at June 30, 2026 was 303,750 of about 519,300, above the threshold. The Q2-26 10-Q page:37 describes it as a "maximum first lien net leverage ratio" and the 10-K had a 30% threshold (page:165). The reported covenant figure is not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. - Waiver: in May 2026 the required lenders conditionally waived the "consolidated net leverage ratio covenant" from the quarter ended March 31, 2026 to the Covenant Waiver Period (page:38). It depends on minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver. The minimum liquidity level is Not supplied. - Going concern: Q2-26 10-Q page:11 states the conditions "raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern", and management’s plans (asset monetization, an equity sale, debt financings) "do not alleviate substantial doubt". The company "does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement" absent the financings. This language is not in the 10-K or the Q1-26 10-Q. - Intralot covenants: a total net leverage ratio not exceeding 4.75:1.00 and a tested senior secured net leverage ratio (page:38); the company was in compliance at June 30, 2026 (page:38). - Subsequent events dated before August 14, 2026: a sterling term facilities agreement of 261.8 million pounds signed July 27, 2026 by Intralot Capital (page:37); a non-binding Bronx loan term sheet in July 2026 (page:11); Fifth Amendment to the Credit Agreement dated July 29, 2026 (page:74), terms Not supplied.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA: issuer measure, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, non-operating items, transaction costs, share-based compensation and other items (Q2-26 release page:5). In the reconciliation it is Adjusted EBITDAR less rent on triple net operating leases (Q2-26 10-Q page:48). It is not a covenant EBITDA; the credit agreement definition is not supplied. - EBITDA in the ratios above means this issuer Adjusted EBITDA. Total debt means contractual principal of all instruments in the debt note, including the revolver and the Bally’s Intralot instruments, and excludes lease liabilities. Net debt deducts unrestricted cash only. - Covenant leverage tests (first lien net) use secured debt only and credit-agreement definitions; the metrics here are total and net consolidated measures and do not equal them.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Bally’s Corporation is a Providence, Rhode Island based operator that the 10-K describes as a global gaming, hospitality, entertainment and technology company. Since February 2025 it has been rebuilt by three transactions: the February 7, 2025 merger with entities affiliated with Standard General and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc.; the October 8, 2025 combination of its International Interactive business with Intralot, which left Bally’s with 57.9% of Bally’s Intralot; and, in 2026, a refinancing and sale-leaseback programme. The business has four reportable segments: Casinos & Resorts, Bally’s Intralot B2B (lottery technology), Bally’s Intralot B2C (online gaming, mainly the UK) and North America Interactive. For a creditor, the structure matters more than the segment mix: ownership is concentrated in one sponsor, the largest growth businesses sit in a subsidiary with its own non-guaranteeing debt group, most casino real estate is leased from GLPI, and two large development projects need capital: Chicago, partly funded by GLPI advances of up to 940.0 million, and the Bronx, whose funding beyond the license fee is not committed. The documented sponsor behaviour is mixed and incomplete: there is no documented priming, uptiering or extraction event in the pages read, and there is also no documented equity injection. The 2025 and 2026 transactions added debt service, fixed rent and project commitments faster than they added reported earnings, which is the mechanism behind the going concern note in the latest filing. This view is a fact pack, not a recovery or relative value judgement.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The February 7, 2025 merger. Bally’s completed merger transactions with SG Parent LLC and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc., an affiliate of Parent (10-K page:7). Public holders received $18.25 per share in cash, Parent and its affiliates then beneficially owned 73.8% of the common stock, and Queen became a wholly owned subsidiary (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Share repurchases of 22,804,384 shares for 416,180 thousand in the Successor period to June 30, 2025 equal the number of shares multiplied by $18.25 (Q2-26 10-Q page:4, page:5; calculation below), which is consistent with the cash consideration; I read it as Analyst Interpretation because the filing does not label the repurchase that way in the pages read. Non-cash consideration issued was 955,647 thousand for the company merger and 555,751 thousand for the Queen merger (Q2-26 10-Q page:6). At closing the company issued $500 million of 11% first lien senior secured notes due October 2, 2028 under a note purchase agreement (10-K page:85); the use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so whether any distribution was debt-funded is Insufficient Information. The notes were repaid in October 2025: Intralot transaction proceeds first paid down 500.0 million of secured debt pro rata across the 2028 Notes and the Term Loan Facility, then an additional payment of 395.0 million settled the remaining 2028 Notes, with a make-whole payment (10-K page:87).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The Intralot transaction. On October 8, 2025 Bally’s completed the transaction under the July 18, 2025 agreement: Intralot paid $1.8 billion in cash and issued about 873.7 million shares for all of Bally’s Holdings Limited, which held the International Interactive business, and Bally’s ownership rose to a controlling 57.9% (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Bally’s assumed Intralot debt of about $1.97 billion principal (10-K page:166). Intralot Capital Luxembourg S.A. is the main borrower: a 400.0 million pound term loan, a 200.0 million euro Greek term loan, a super senior revolver with 160.0 million euros of commitments, 600.0 million euros of 6.75% fixed notes and 300.0 million euros of floating notes (Q2-26 10-Q page:31 to page:37). Parent group debt is not guaranteed by Bally’s Intralot, and Bally’s Intralot debt carries its own covenants (a total net leverage ratio not exceeding 4.75:1.00) (Q2-26 10-Q page:11, page:38).

facts.text: The 2026 refinancing and sale-leaseback. On February 11, 2026 the company entered into $1.1 billion of senior secured 2026 Term Loans: Term SOFR (3.0% floor) plus 7.5%, with up to 3.5% payable in kind, secured pari passu with the revolver, due February 11, 2031, or March 1, 2029 if the 2029 Notes remain outstanding on that date (Q2-26 10-Q page:34, page:32). A revolver drawing of $448.0 million made in January 2026 for the New York license fee was repaid in February 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:66).

rows.label: Bally’s is a controlled gaming company that grew by acquisition into casinos, lottery technology and online gaming. A sponsor holds 67.1%, a 57.9% owned subsidiary carries separate debt, and a large project remains unfunded.

The 2026 term loans pay Term SOFR plus 7.5%, and the Bally’s Twin River sale-leaseback added 56.0 million of annual rent.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Bally's Corp is a weak, stressed credit whose debt exceeds what its earnings can carry without new financing. Its strongest support is a diversified, licensed operating base that produced Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million over the last twelve months to June 30, 2026, and a lender group that has granted a conditional covenant waiver. The weakest point is liquidity: debt of USD 4,910.1 million is 9.57x Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest only 1.15x, operations used cash, and the latest filing states substantial doubt about going concern. The outcome will be decided by whether asset sales, an equity sale or new debt close before the waiver conditions and the October 2026 revolver reduction bind, and by what the controlling sponsor does. Nothing after August 14, 2026 is supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is high on every measure available and rests on a non-GAAP earnings measure. Total debt of USD 4,910.1 million is 9.57x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million, and net of unrestricted cash of USD 390.2 million it is 8.81x [CP-1 leverage chart data]. The ratio rose from 8.88x at September 30, 2025, although the intervening perimeter changes mean it is indicative rather than like-for-like [CP-1 Financial base view]. Operating lease liabilities of USD 2,392.3 million sit outside this debt figure and the fixed rent is deducted inside Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 financials table].

facts.text: Cash earnings are almost fully absorbed by financing and rent. Cash interest of USD 444.6 million is 86.7% of Adjusted EBITDA, so Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.15x. Adding the triple net rent expense of USD 210.0 million to cash interest, Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 722.8 million covers the total 1.10x. The 2026 term loans cost at least USD 105.4 million a year even at the 3.0% floor plus the lower 6.5% base-rate margin, and more under the 7.5% Term SOFR margin, and part of the interest may be paid in kind [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 335.7 million over the last twelve months [CP-1 financials table].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is the decisive issue. Cash of USD 390.2 million and reported revolver availability of USD 195.8 million total USD 586.0 million, compared with a six-month free cash outflow (operating cash flow less capital expenditures and capitalized software) of USD 359.1 million [CP-1 liquidity chart data; Q2 2026 10-Q page:5]. Whether the reduction occurred, and how it was met, is Not supplied because the pack ends at August 14, 2026.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Covenant protection exists only through a conditional waiver. In May 2026 the required lenders conditionally waived the consolidated net leverage ratio covenant for each quarter from March 31, 2026 until the earlier of the company’s election or the day before the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2027, subject to minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver [Q2 2026 10-Q page:38]. The company states that it does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement or the reinstated covenant absent the financings under discussion, and that substantial doubt about going concern exists [Q2 2026 10-Q page:11]. The waiver level and the reported ratio are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable.

Parent-group debt is USD 2,898.3 million: USD 1,413.3 million of first lien revolver and 2026 term loans and USD 1,485.0 million of senior notes. Bally’s Intralot debt is USD 2,011.8 million, and Bally’s Intralot does not guarantee the parent’s debt [CP-1 debt table; CP-1A Transaction summary]. The two Intralot-linked segments produced USD 86.7 million of Q2 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDAR, leaving USD 37.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA from casinos, North America Interactive and corporate cost after rent [Q2 2026 10-Q page:48]. rows.label: Bally's is a weak, stressed credit: debt is 9.57x Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.15x, and the latest filing states substantial doubt about going concern. The outcome turns on unfinished financings and sponsor action.
Gross debt was USD 4,910.1 million, 9.57x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million; net leverage was 8.81x.
Cash interest took 86.7% of Adjusted EBITDA, and earnings cover cash interest plus rent only 1.10x.
Cash and reported revolver availability were USD 586.0 million at June 30, 2026, against a six-month free cash outflow of USD 359.1 million.
The revolver covenant is waived only conditionally, and management states substantial doubt about going concern.
Parent-group debt is USD 2,898.3 million against USD 2,011.8 million at Bally’s Intralot, which gives no guarantee. Q2 2026 earnings outside the Intralot segments were USD 37.4 million.
Weak and stressed fundamental credit: leverage of 9.57x, cover of 1.15x, negative operating cash flow and a going concern warning; near-term outcome depends on financing execution and the waiver

Thesis: a diversified, licensed gaming business has been levered and expanded faster than its cash earnings, so creditors depend on refinancing, asset sales and sponsor action rather than on free cash flow

## Request

- Issuer: Bally's Corp (issuer id `baly`; the filings name the registrant "Bally’s Corporation", NYSE: BALY), as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05, reporting currency USD, current period Q2 2026, prior period FY2025 (context).
- Run: `baly-2026-11-05-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`. Requested downstream modules: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the launcher's `minimum` set). CP-0 runs first as their dependency.
- Execution: host session. The analyst searched all seven pinned page files by term and read the chunks cited below in full; chunks not cited were not read in full. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied filings and releases support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and what remains blocked?

- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This answer gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and normalizes, reconciles and calculates nothing.

Short labels used below: 10-K = FY2025 annual report; Q3-25 10-Q, Q1-26 10-Q, Q2-26 10-Q = the quarterly reports; Q4-25 release, Q1-26 release, Q2-26 release = the three Exhibit 99.1 files.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases support all four requested analyses with stated limits. The latest quarterly report carries a going concern warning and a covenant waiver, so downstream work must treat liquidity as the central issue. | Medium | No credit agreement, waiver, amendment or filing after the August 14, 2026 quarterly report is supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The June 30, 2026 quarterly report states substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern and describes a conditional lender waiver. | Debt and liquidity analysis must start from the waiver conditions and the unfinished financing plans. | High |

| Reported 2025 figures are split between a Predecessor and a Successor period around the February 7, 2025 merger. | Annual and trailing comparisons need explicit period labels and cannot be read as one clean year. | High |

| Debt sits at both the parent group and the majority-owned Bally’s Intralot, which does not guarantee parent debt. | Debt must be kept by borrower group before any consolidated leverage view is used. | Medium |
| Waiver terms, credit agreement amendments and filings after mid-August 2026 are not supplied. | Covenant headroom and later events cannot be verified from this pack. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four requested consumers. Audited annual statements, three sets of interim statements and three earnings releases are located, with debt, liquidity, covenant, segment and cash-flow notes. The limits are three. First, the filings are the controlling authority and the releases are attributed management claims. Second, the 2025 comparatives are split into Successor and Predecessor periods. Third, executed credit documents and any event after the August 14, 2026 report are not supplied. Source sufficiency is not completion of downstream analysis; CP-OS sequences that.
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Annual, interim and segment statements, debt and maturity tables, cash paid for interest and Adjusted EBITDA are located. 2025 columns are split by the merger date, and the Q4-25 release is preliminary. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, segments, the February 2025 merger, the Intralot transaction, the sale-leaseback and the pending evoke offer are described in the filings and releases. Transaction agreements are not supplied. |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Debt note, covenant text, waiver description, going concern note and liquidity discussion are located. Executed credit documents, the minimum liquidity level and post-June 30, 2026 financing outcomes are not supplied. |
| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every source has stable chunk numbers, so claims can be traced. Extraction is text only, so table layout and images are not inspected. |
Command sheet: CP-1 RUN; CP-1A RUN; CP-2 RUN; CP-5 RUN. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED: no critical identity boundary is unresolved and no source has blocked preparation.
### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited statements and the debt note. page:1 "FORM 10-K"; page:1 "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025". Signed page:203 "on March 23, 2026".

- Audit: page:102 states an unqualified opinion on the financial statements and refers to an adverse opinion on internal control: "expressed an adverse opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting because of a material weakness". Management's description is at page:51: "identified a material weakness as of December 31, 2025".

- Periods: the statements are split by the merger. page:102 "from February 8, 2025 to December 31, 2025 (successor), from January 1, 2025 to February 7, 2025 (predecessor), and for the year ended December 31, 2024 (predecessor)". There is no single full-year 2025 column.

- Statements located: balance sheet page:106 and page:107; cash flows page:109 and page:110, including page:110 "Cash paid for interest, net of amounts capitalized $340,739 $39,069 $314,245"; debt note page:162; maturities page:170; covenant text page:165; segment Adjusted EBITDAR and consolidated Adjusted EBITDA page:80 ("Adjusted EBITDA 478,009 24,390 495,611"); liquidity discussion from page:82; segment note page:187.
- Units: statements in thousands, MD&A summary in millions (page:75 "Total revenue $2,436.2 $220.5 $2,450.5"). USD.

- Family and authority: filed, unaudited quarterly report; supplies the discrete Q3 2025 quarter. page:3 "Three Months Ended September 30, 2025 Period from February 8, 2025 to September 30, 2025 Period from January 1, 2025 to February 7, 2025".

- Located: balance sheet page:2; cash flow supplement page:6 ("Cash paid for interest, net of amounts capitalized $ 243,341 $ 39,069 $ 256,161"); debt note page:38; covenant text page:41; segment note from page:50; Adjusted EBITDA page:70; liquidity from page:73.

- Version relationship: superseded for the balance sheet by later reports, but the only source for discrete Q3 2025 operations and the September 30, 2025 balance sheet. Keep it as a separate active source.
- Family and authority: filed, unaudited. page:3 "Three Months Ended March 31, 2026 Period from February 8, 2025 to March 31, 2025 Period from January 1, 2025 to February 7, 2025".

- Located: balance sheet page:2 (page:2 "Long-term debt, net 4,389,903 4,463,313"); cash flow page:5 including cash paid for interest; debt note page:39; maturities page:48; covenant text page:42; waiver page:43; Adjusted EBITDA page:71; liquidity from page:71.
- The waiver is already described here. This report contains no going concern language (search for "substantial doubt" across all seven sources finds it only in the Q2-26 10-Q).
- Family and authority: filed, unaudited; the latest periodic report, signed August 14, 2026 (page:75 "on August 14, 2026"). Controls the June 30, 2026 balance sheet and the going concern disclosure.
- Basis: page:10 "a Predecessor period, which includes the period from January 1, 2025 through February 7, 2025". The Successor period runs from February 8, 2025.

- Located: balance sheet page:2; operations page:3; equity page:4 and page:5; cash flows page:5 and page:6; going concern and plans page:11; debt note page:31 to page:38; segment note page:47 and page:48; MD&A from page:51 (consolidated Adjusted EBITDA at page:60, page:60 "Adjusted EBITDA 124,034 129,246 247,318 212,517 24,390"); liquidity page:62 to page:65; risk factor addition page:74; exhibit index page:74 and page:75.
- Units: thousands, USD. Foreign-currency debt is shown with principal currency at page:32.
#### Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1)
- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished as exhibits; management-prepared, unaudited, attributed claims. They do not override the filings.

- Q4-25 release: page:1 "reported preliminary financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2025" and page:2 "The Company will file an extension for the filing of its Annual Report on Form 10-K". Its preliminary status means the 10-K controls. The Form 12b-25 it mentions is not supplied.
- Q1-26 release: dated May 18, 2026; page:1 "Consolidated revenue of $755.7 million increased 28.3% year over year".

- Q2-26 release: dated August 14, 2026. It adds a pro forma combined view of Bally’s and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc. for six months 2025 (page:7 "Successor Pro Forma Combined(1)"), swap and hedge footnotes (page:9) and triple net lease cash payments (page:8 "Cash payments associated with triple net operating leases(2) 133,561 69,983 14,877"). Its text says reconciliations are in the tables below, but only segment Adjusted EBITDAR and revenue tables appear in the extracted text; the reconciliation to net loss is in the Q2-26 10-Q at page:48.

- Version relationship: the Q2-26 release repeats statement facts from the 10-Q (for example page:8 "Long-term debt, including current portion 4,506,700 4,500,657", also at Q2-26 10-Q page:31). It is not independent corroboration. The 10-Q controls.
### Information-availability boundary
- All sources are dated on or before August 14, 2026, before the as-of date and cutoff of 2026-11-05.

- Nothing dated between August 14, 2026 and 2026-11-05 is supplied. The Q2-26 10-Q refers to a Form 8-K filed on August 5, 2026 (page:74 "Fifth Amendment to Credit Agreement, dated as of July 29, 2026"). Neither that 8-K nor its exhibit is supplied. Any Q3 2026 results, financing outcome, equity sale or evoke closing are therefore Not supplied, not absent.

- Subsequent events inside the Q2-26 10-Q are dated before August 14, 2026 and are usable as disclosed: page:37 "On July 27, 2026, Bally’s Intralot" signed a sterling term facility; page:11 "In July 2026, the Company executed a term sheet" for a Bally’s Bronx loan, described as non-binding.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Bally’s Corporation, Delaware, consolidated with non-controlling interests. Bally’s Intralot S.A. is majority owned and consolidated: page:8 of the Q2-26 10-Q "the Company’s ownership of Bally’s Intralot increased to a controlling 57.9% interest".

- Predecessor and Successor: the February 7, 2025 merger with SG Parent LLC and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc. created a push-down basis. Q2-26 10-Q page:10: "the results of operations, financial position and cash flows of the Predecessor and the Successor are not directly comparable".

- Debt borrower groups (Q2-26 10-Q page:31 to page:37): the parent group (2026 Term Loans, Revolving Credit Facility, 5.625% Senior Notes due 2029, 5.875% Senior Notes due 2031) and the Bally’s Intralot group (Intralot British Term Loan, Greek Term Loan, Greek Retail Bond, Revolving Credit Facility, Fixed and Floating Rate Notes, Supplemental Indenture, borrower Intralot Capital Luxembourg S.A.). page:11: "Bally’s Intralot does not guarantee any of Bally’s Corporation’s debt." The reverse relationship, whether parent group debt is guaranteed by Intralot entities, is stated only for the Senior Notes guarantors at page:32 ("guaranteed, jointly and severally, by certain of the Company’s restricted subsidiaries"). The full guarantor list and restricted or unrestricted designations are not supplied.

- Lease counterparty: GLPI leases many properties (Q2-26 10-Q page:7 footnote "Properties leased from Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc."). Lease liabilities are on the balance sheet outside Long-term debt (page:2 "Long-term portion of lease liabilities 2,265,504 1,829,190").
- The context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank. That is not evidence of their absence.
### Strongest contrary evidence and conflicts

- Going concern. Q2-26 10-Q page:11: "raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern", and "management’s plans do not alleviate substantial doubt". The Q1-26 10-Q and the 10-K do not carry this language. The evidence is a change between filings, not a conflict; downstream modules must date it to the June 30, 2026 report.

- Covenant description. The waiver is called a waiver of the "consolidated net leverage ratio covenant" at Q2-26 10-Q page:11 and page:38, while the covenant description at page:37 is a "maximum first lien net leverage ratio" tested when utilization exceeds 25% of commitments. The same page:38 later refers to the "consolidated first lien net leverage ratio covenant". The 10-K threshold was 30% (page:165 "exceed 30% of"). The wording difference is unresolved without the Credit Agreement and waiver, and CP-2 must carry it as a gap, not choose a definition.

- Revolver capacity. Q2-26 10-Q page:33: "there was $195.8 million available under the Company’s Revolving Credit Facility" and availability "will be further reduced to approximately $319 million" from October 2026. The same page states a total reduced commitment of about $519.3 million in February 2026. The balance sheet debt table shows Revolving Credit Facility 303,750 outstanding at page:31. Any liquidity consumer must keep these separate and must not infer letters of credit.

- Carrying amount versus principal. Page:31 "Long-term debt, including current portion 4,506,700 4,500,657" is after discount and a fair value adjustment, while page:37 maturities total "$ 4,910,068". The two are different bases, not a conflict; the note footnote (3) at page:32 explains the fair value adjustment.

- 10-K internal wording. The risk factor summary at page:20 refers to "material weaknesses" while the body at page:51 describes "a material weakness". The count is unresolved from text; the adverse internal control opinion at page:102 is unambiguous.

- Preliminary release versus 10-K. The Q4-25 release is labelled preliminary and announces an extension for the 10-K, which was signed March 23, 2026. Revenue of $2,436,189 thousand for the Successor period in the release (page:2 "Total $ 746,245 $ 580,365 $ 2,436,189 $ 220,498 $ 2,450,478") matches the 10-K MD&A summary of $2,436.2 million (page:75). No conflict found on revenue; other release figures must be checked against the 10-K before use.
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Statements, segments, debt by instrument, maturities, cash paid for interest, Adjusted EBITDA | 10-K page:106 to page:110, page:162, page:170; Q3-25 10-Q page:2, page:38; Q1-26 10-Q page:2, page:5, page:39, page:48; Q2-26 10-Q page:2 to page:6, page:31 to page:37, page:47 to page:48, page:60 | Successor and Predecessor split; Q2 2025 three-month comparatives come only from the Q2-26 10-Q and its release; Q4-25 release preliminary; Adjusted EBITDA is issuer non-GAAP |

| CP-1A | Business, segments, history, ownership, transactions | 10-K page:9; Q2-26 10-Q page:6 to page:8; Q2-26 release page:1 to page:4; Q4-25 release page:1 | Merger Agreement, Intralot Transaction Agreement, evoke offer documents and sale-leaseback agreement not supplied |

| CP-2 | Liquidity, covenants, waiver, lease burden, going concern, financing plans | Q2-26 10-Q page:11, page:33, page:37 to page:38, page:62 to page:65, page:74; Q1-26 10-Q page:42 to page:43; 10-K page:165 | Credit Agreement, Amendments No. 3 to No. 5, Conditional Waiver, 2026 Term Loan agreement, indentures not supplied; minimum liquidity level not located in the text |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims in every source | All sources carry chunk numbers | Text extraction only; no table-layout or image check; no external or market data supplied |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: audited FY2025 statements, interim statements to June 30, 2026 and the Q3 2025 comparatives are located in the filings. Debt, maturities, cash paid for interest, segments and consolidated Adjusted EBITDA are all in the Q2-26 10-Q, so a trailing view to June 30, 2026 can be built from filed figures once period labels are kept separate.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the Q2-26 10-Q page:11 states that the company "does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement". The mechanism: a reduction in revolver availability from October 2026 and the end of the covenant waiver require financing that is not yet committed, so a downstream consumer that reads only reported covenant compliance at June 30, 2026 (page:38 "the Company was in compliance with all covenants under its debt agreements") would overstate near-term headroom.

- Source risk mechanism: the Successor and Predecessor split and the Intralot consolidation break like-for-like comparison. A consumer that sums or subtracts across the merger date, or reads consolidated debt as one borrower group, mixes bases.

- What cannot proceed from this pack alone: covenant headroom against the executed definitions, waiver condition testing, guarantor-level or restricted-group analysis, and any view of events after August 14, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Credit Agreement with Amendments No. 3, No. 4 and No. 5, the Conditional Waiver dated May 14, 2026, the 2026 Term Loan Credit Facility agreement, the Senior Notes Indenture, the Form 8-K of August 5, 2026 and every later 8-K and the Q3 2026 report if filed before the cutoff.
## Calculations
No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Figures quoted above are printed in the sources with their locators.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Credit Agreement, Amendments No. 3 to No. 5, Conditional Waiver, 2026 Term Loan agreement and indentures not supplied; minimum liquidity level and waiver conditions not located in the text | High | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the executed documents (Q2-26 10-Q page:74 lists them as exhibits or incorporated exhibits) |

| Nothing dated after August 14, 2026 supplied; the August 5, 2026 Form 8-K and any Q3 2026 report or financing outcome are Not supplied | High | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply later 8-Ks and the Q3 2026 report if filed on or before 2026-11-05 |

| Successor and Predecessor periods are not comparable; no single full-year 2025 column | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Keep period labels explicit; use the Q2-26 release pro forma combined view only as labelled non-GAAP |

| Bally’s Intralot debt and parent group debt sit in separate borrower groups; full guarantor and restricted or unrestricted detail not supplied | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Supply guarantor schedules and Intralot group financial statements |
| Covenant naming differs across the Q2-26 10-Q (net leverage versus first lien net leverage; 25% versus 30% trigger in the 10-K) | Medium | CP-2 | Confirm against the Credit Agreement and waiver |
| Q4-25 release is preliminary and the Form 12b-25 is not supplied | Low | CP-1 | Use the 10-K as controlling |
| Merger, Intralot, sale-leaseback, evoke and GLPI lease agreements not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the agreements or rely on filed descriptions with that limit |
| Text extraction only; no original HTML, XBRL or image inspection | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML |
| No ratings, market prices or peer data | Low for the selected modules | CP-2 | Keep Not supplied |
## Next module

- CP-1: use the 10-K and 10-Q statements as controlling and the releases as attributed support. Keep Successor and Predecessor columns separate, keep parent group and Bally’s Intralot debt separate, keep lease liabilities outside debt, and label Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR as issuer non-GAAP.

- CP-1A: carry the February 7, 2025 merger, the October 8, 2025 Intralot Transaction, the 2026 Bally’s Twin River (Lincoln) sale-leaseback, the New York license and the evoke offer as the central transactions, citing the filings. Label anything after August 14, 2026 as Not supplied.
- CP-2: start from the going concern note, the waiver conditions and the October 2026 revolver reduction. Carry the covenant naming difference and the missing minimum liquidity level as gaps.
- CP-5: check each claim against the cited chunk, and carry the limitation that no agreement and no post-August 14, 2026 filing is supplied.

### Liquidity and covenant facts

- Revolver: commitments were reduced to about 519.3 million in February 2026; from October 2026 total availability falls to about 319 million; 195.8 million was available at June 30, 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:33). Commitments less borrowings is 215.55 million, so 19.75 million of commitments is neither drawn nor reported as available; the filing does not say why, and letters of credit are not named.

- Financial covenant: when utilization exceeds 25% of commitments, the revolver requires "a first lien secured net indebtedness to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of 4.00 to 1.00" (Q2-26 10-Q page:65). Utilization at June 30, 2026 was 303,750 of about 519,300, above the threshold. The Q2-26 10-Q page:37 describes it as a "maximum first lien net leverage ratio" and the 10-K had a 30% threshold (page:165). The reported covenant figure is not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable.

- Waiver: in May 2026 the required lenders conditionally waived the "consolidated net leverage ratio covenant" from the quarter ended March 31, 2026 to the Covenant Waiver Period (page:38). It depends on minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver. The minimum liquidity level is Not supplied.

- Going concern: Q2-26 10-Q page:11 states the conditions "raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern", and management’s plans (asset monetization, an equity sale, debt financings) "do not alleviate substantial doubt". The company "does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement" absent the financings. This language is not in the 10-K or the Q1-26 10-Q.
- Intralot covenants: a total net leverage ratio not exceeding 4.75:1.00 and a tested senior secured net leverage ratio (page:38); the company was in compliance at June 30, 2026 (page:38).

- Subsequent events dated before August 14, 2026: a sterling term facilities agreement of 261.8 million pounds signed July 27, 2026 by Intralot Capital (page:37); a non-binding Bronx loan term sheet in July 2026 (page:11); Fifth Amendment to the Credit Agreement dated July 29, 2026 (page:74), terms Not supplied.
### Definition review

- Adjusted EBITDA: issuer measure, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, non-operating items, transaction costs, share-based compensation and other items (Q2-26 release page:5). In the reconciliation it is Adjusted EBITDAR less rent on triple net operating leases (Q2-26 10-Q page:48). It is not a covenant EBITDA; the credit agreement definition is not supplied.

- EBITDA in the ratios above means this issuer Adjusted EBITDA. Total debt means contractual principal of all instruments in the debt note, including the revolver and the Bally’s Intralot instruments, and excludes lease liabilities. Net debt deducts unrestricted cash only.
- Covenant leverage tests (first lien net) use secured debt only and credit-agreement definitions; the metrics here are total and net consolidated measures and do not equal them.

### Business and transaction view

Bally’s Corporation is a Providence, Rhode Island based operator that the 10-K describes as a global gaming, hospitality, entertainment and technology company. Since February 2025 it has been rebuilt by three transactions: the February 7, 2025 merger with entities affiliated with Standard General and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc.; the October 8, 2025 combination of its International Interactive business with Intralot, which left Bally’s with 57.9% of Bally’s Intralot; and, in 2026, a refinancing and sale-leaseback programme. The business has four reportable segments: Casinos & Resorts, Bally’s Intralot B2B (lottery technology), Bally’s Intralot B2C (online gaming, mainly the UK) and North America Interactive. For a creditor, the structure matters more than the segment mix: ownership is concentrated in one sponsor, the largest growth businesses sit in a subsidiary with its own non-guaranteeing debt group, most casino real estate is leased from GLPI, and two large development projects need capital: Chicago, partly funded by GLPI advances of up to 940.0 million, and the Bronx, whose funding beyond the license fee is not committed. The documented sponsor behaviour is mixed and incomplete: there is no documented priming, uptiering or extraction event in the pages read, and there is also no documented equity injection. The 2025 and 2026 transactions added debt service, fixed rent and project commitments faster than they added reported earnings, which is the mechanism behind the going concern note in the latest filing. This view is a fact pack, not a recovery or relative value judgement.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The February 7, 2025 merger. Bally’s completed merger transactions with SG Parent LLC and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc., an affiliate of Parent (10-K page:7). Public holders received $18.25 per share in cash, Parent and its affiliates then beneficially owned 73.8% of the common stock, and Queen became a wholly owned subsidiary (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Share repurchases of 22,804,384 shares for 416,180 thousand in the Successor period to June 30, 2025 equal the number of shares multiplied by $18.25 (Q2-26 10-Q page:4, page:5; calculation below), which is consistent with the cash consideration; I read it as Analyst Interpretation because the filing does not label the repurchase that way in the pages read. Non-cash consideration issued was 955,647 thousand for the company merger and 555,751 thousand for the Queen merger (Q2-26 10-Q page:6). At closing the company issued $500 million of 11% first lien senior secured notes due October 2, 2028 under a note purchase agreement (10-K page:85); the use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so whether any distribution was debt-funded is Insufficient Information. The notes were repaid in October 2025: Intralot transaction proceeds first paid down 500.0 million of secured debt pro rata across the 2028 Notes and the Term Loan Facility, then an additional payment of 395.0 million settled the remaining 2028 Notes, with a make-whole payment (10-K page:87).

The Intralot transaction. On October 8, 2025 Bally’s completed the transaction under the July 18, 2025 agreement: Intralot paid $1.8 billion in cash and issued about 873.7 million shares for all of Bally’s Holdings Limited, which held the International Interactive business, and Bally’s ownership rose to a controlling 57.9% (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). It was accounted for as an equity transaction with a 42.1% non-controlling interest and no gain or loss (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Bally’s assumed Intralot debt of about $1.97 billion principal (10-K page:166). Intralot Capital Luxembourg S.A. is the main borrower: a 400.0 million pound term loan, a 200.0 million euro Greek term loan, a super senior revolver with 160.0 million euros of commitments, 600.0 million euros of 6.75% fixed notes and 300.0 million euros of floating notes (Q2-26 10-Q page:31 to page:37). Parent group debt is not guaranteed by Bally’s Intralot, and Bally’s Intralot debt carries its own covenants (a total net leverage ratio not exceeding 4.75:1.00) (Q2-26 10-Q page:11, page:38).

The 2026 refinancing and sale-leaseback. On February 11, 2026 the company entered into $1.1 billion of senior secured 2026 Term Loans: Term SOFR (3.0% floor) plus 7.5%, with up to 3.5% payable in kind, secured pari passu with the revolver, due February 11, 2031, or March 1, 2029 if the 2029 Notes remain outstanding on that date (Q2-26 10-Q page:34, page:32). It repaid the previous Term Loan Facility in full, paying $1.48 billion and recognising a $63.4 million loss on extinguishment (Q2-26 10-Q page:33). The same day it sold the Bally’s Twin River land and real estate to GLPI for total consideration of $700.0 million, leased it back under Master Lease No. 2, and agreed 56.0 million of added annual rent; it recorded a gain of $105.8 million (Q2-26 10-Q page:39). Revolver commitments fell by 22.5% to about $519.3 million, with the revolver maturity split into October 2026 and October 2028 tranches and total availability falling to about $319 million from October 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:33, page:66). A revolver drawing of $448.0 million made in January 2026 for the New York license fee was repaid in February 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:66).

Covenant relief and amendments. In May 2026 the required revolving lenders conditionally waived compliance with the consolidated net leverage ratio covenant from the quarter ended March 31, 2026 until the earlier of the company’s certification election or the day before delivery of the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2027; the waiver is conditioned on minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver (Q2-26 10-Q page:38). A Fourth Amendment dated May 5, 2026 raised revolver margins (Q2-26 10-Q page:64, page:74); a Fifth Amendment dated July 29, 2026 is listed as incorporated from a Form 8-K of August 5, 2026 whose terms are Not supplied (Q2-26 10-Q page:74). The Q2-26 10-Q states the company does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement or the reinstated covenant over the next twelve months absent the financings under discussion (page:11).

Development and licence commitments. The company was awarded a New York downstate gaming license in December 2025 and paid the $500.0 million license fee in the first quarter of 2026, plus a $115 million golf course concession contingent payment (Q2-26 10-Q page:44; Q2-26 release page:2). A conveyance arrangement recorded a liability of $183.6 million for specified capital improvements (Q2-26 10-Q page:25), with improvements of approximately $161.0 million required (page:44). The Bronx project is described as a $4.0 billion integrated casino project expected to open by 2030 (Q2-26 release page:2, management language), and a bond or cash deposit equal to 5% of total project investment is required (Q2-26 10-Q page:44). Chicago: the permanent casino targets opening in early 2027 on management’s account (Q2-26 release page:2); GLPI has committed to advance up to $940.0 million of hard costs in exchange for added rent of 8.5% of advances, on top of 20.0 million initial annual rent (Q2-26 10-Q page:70). In the Las Vegas site, the Athletics stadium is slated for completion before the 2028 season (Q2-26 release page:2).

Investments and acquisitions. In April 2025 the company committed A$200 million in convertible notes and subordinated debt for an approximately 38% economic interest in The Star Entertainment Group Limited (10-K page:6); it now holds a 37.7% equity interest (Q2-26 10-Q page:15). Bally’s Intralot agreed in June 2026 to acquire evoke plc, with a cooperation agreement dated June 5, 2026 (Q2-26 release page:1; Q2-26 10-Q page:74). The consideration, financing and approvals timetable are Not supplied; since the buyer is Bally’s Intralot, which does not guarantee parent debt, any financing sits with the Intralot group unless otherwise documented, which is an Analyst Interpretation. Bally’s Intralot also signed a total return equity swap on June 15, 2026 over its own shares for up to 50.0 million euros (Q2-26 10-Q page:28).

Subsequent events and new debt after the quarter. Bally’s Intralot, through Intralot Capital, signed a sterling term facilities agreement for 261.8 million pounds on July 27, 2026, drawn in two three-year tranches (Q2-26 10-Q page:37). In July 2026 the company signed a non-binding term sheet for a loan to fund the Bally’s Bronx project and general corporate purposes (Q2-26 10-Q page:11), and in August 2026 a letter of intent with a potential equity investor (Q2-26 release page:2, management language). No later event is supplied.
### Governance and sponsor behaviour

- Supportive: no documented equity contribution, shareholder loan or guarantee by Standard General is in the pages read. The company discloses reporting on the waiver and going concern in a filed 10-Q. Evidence quality: High (primary and dated). Dimensions: sponsor alignment; transparency.

- Neutral or Mixed: the merger was with a sponsor affiliate (Queen) for non-cash consideration of 555,751 thousand, and the merger closed alongside a $500 million 11% secured note; funding and fees to the sponsor are not stated. Documented minority leakage at Intralot: a dividend of 17,644 thousand to Bally’s Intralot minority holders (paid July 27, 2026) and incremental Intralot share purchases of 24,359 thousand in six months (Q2-26 10-Q page:4, page:5), both small against the 4,910,068 thousand debt (CP-1). Dimensions: capital allocation; related-party flows.

- Extraction-Oriented or Creditor-Adverse: no dividend recapitalisation, priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release is documented in the pages read. The company says it paid no cash dividends in the periods presented (Q2-26 10-Q page:63). The 2026 Term Loans are secured pari passu with the revolver and rank on the same collateral, and the waiver restricts additional secured debt (page:34, page:38).

- Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility are separate. Capacity: the debt documents limit restricted payments and indebtedness (Q2-26 10-Q page:37), and the Rhode Island regulatory agreement restricts payments above its 5.50 to 1.00 trigger (10-K page:16). Willingness: no distribution to the sponsor is documented. Feasibility: operating cash flow is negative and liquidity is described as insufficient absent financings (Q2-26 10-Q page:5, page:11).

- Reporting discipline: an adverse internal control opinion, preliminary results with a 10-K extension, and a going concern note are documented (10-K page:102; Q4-25 release page:2; Q2-26 10-Q page:11).
### Credit translations

- Evidence: Standard General holds 67.1% and the Executive Chairman is its principal (10-K page:66). Risk mechanic: a controlling holder decides whether to inject equity, sell assets or hold, and the company says an equity sale is among its plans (Q2-26 10-Q page:11). Credit implication: the going concern note makes the sponsor’s response the main uncertainty, and there is no documented commitment either way. Counter-evidence: no conflict logged.

- Evidence: Bally’s Intralot does not guarantee parent debt while its cash flows are consolidated (Q2-26 10-Q page:11). Risk mechanic: reported earnings and cash include a subsidiary whose creditors rank first against its assets, and 42.1% of its equity belongs to others. Credit implication: parent-group leverage is higher than the consolidated 9.57x implies on the share of earnings that cannot be moved up. This reading is Analyst Interpretation; the intercompany restrictions are Not supplied.

- Evidence: the Twin River sale-leaseback added 56.0 million of annual rent against 700.0 million of consideration (Q2-26 10-Q page:39). Risk mechanic: property value was converted into a fixed rent claim ahead of the debt. Credit implication: fixed charge cover is lower than the CP-1 interest cover suggests, because rent sits in Adjusted EBITDA as a deduction and is not shown in interest.

- Evidence: UK gaming tax and cost ratios (Q2-26 release page:3; Q2-26 10-Q page:57). Risk mechanic: a tax increase on the largest interactive market reduces cash conversion. Credit implication: revenue growth is not a reliable indicator of debt service capacity. Counter-evidence: the 5.50 to 1.00 trigger in the Rhode Island agreement has no logged conflict but is untested.
- Key uncertainties: waiver conditions, minimum liquidity level, outcome of the financings under discussion, evoke terms, funding of Bronx and Chicago, and regulatory leverage definitions.
### Conflicts logged (not reconciled)

- Intralot consideration. 10-K page:7: "Intralot paid the Company €1.5 million ($1.8 billion) in cash"; Q2-26 10-Q page:8: "Bally’s Intralot paid the Company $1.8 billion in cash"; Q4-25 release page:1 gives the Intralot transaction as "€2.7 billion consisting of cash and stock consideration". The 10-K euro figure is inconsistent with its own dollar figure; the sources are not reconciled. Effect: the cash proceeds used for debt repayment are taken as $1.8 billion from the dollar figures, and the euro figure is flagged for review.

- Casino count. Q2-26 release page:6: "20 casinos across 11 U.S. states and one casino in Newcastle, UK"; Q2-26 10-Q page:53: "we own and operate 20 casinos globally, including in the United Kingdom". The release count is one higher than the 10-Q if read literally.

- Covenant name. Q2-26 10-Q page:38 names the waived test "consolidated net leverage ratio covenant" and later "consolidated first lien net leverage ratio covenant"; page:65 describes a "first lien secured net indebtedness to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of 4.00 to 1.00". Not reconciled without the credit agreement.
- Ownership percentage: 73.8% at the merger date (Q2-26 10-Q page:8) and 67.1% at February 28, 2026 (10-K page:66) are at different dates; no conflict, and the change is unexplained.
- Material weakness count: "material weaknesses" (10-K page:20) and "a material weakness" (10-K page:51).
## Calculations
- Merger cash consideration check: 22,804,384 shares × $18.25 = $416,180,008, against share repurchases of 416,180 thousand (Q2-26 10-Q page:4, page:5, page:8). Equal within rounding.
- Sale-leaseback rent yield on consideration: 56.0 / 700.0 = 8.0% (Q2-26 10-Q page:39). This is annual added rent over total consideration, not a cap rate.

- Chicago added rent at full GLPI advances: 940.0 × 8.5% = 79.9; plus initial annual rent of 20.0 gives 99.9 per year before escalation (Q2-26 10-Q page:70). Terms-based; actual advances to date are lower, and 274,034 thousand were received in six months 2026 (page:40).
- Bally’s Bronx security: 5% × total project investment; with a project cost of 4.0 billion this would be 200.0 million. The filing does not state the base used; Not calculable from filed terms.
- Gaming expense ratios: 52% and 43% as printed (Q2-26 10-Q page:57); not recalculated.
- Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA figures are reused from the CP-1 handoff without change.

### Credit view

Bally's Corp is a weak, stressed credit whose debt exceeds what its earnings can carry without new financing. Its strongest support is a diversified, licensed operating base that produced Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million over the last twelve months to June 30, 2026, and a lender group that has granted a conditional covenant waiver. The weakest point is liquidity: debt of USD 4,910.1 million is 9.57x Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest only 1.15x, operations used cash, and the latest filing states substantial doubt about going concern. The outcome will be decided by whether asset sales, an equity sale or new debt close before the waiver conditions and the October 2026 revolver reduction bind, and by what the controlling sponsor does. Nothing after August 14, 2026 is supplied.
### Key findings

Leverage is high on every measure available and rests on a non-GAAP earnings measure. Total debt of USD 4,910.1 million is 9.57x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million, and net of unrestricted cash of USD 390.2 million it is 8.81x [CP-1 leverage chart data]. The ratio rose from 8.88x at September 30, 2025, although the intervening perimeter changes mean it is indicative rather than like-for-like [CP-1 Financial base view]. Operating lease liabilities of USD 2,392.3 million sit outside this debt figure and the fixed rent is deducted inside Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 financials table].

Cash earnings are almost fully absorbed by financing and rent. Cash interest of USD 444.6 million is 86.7% of Adjusted EBITDA, so Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.15x. Adding the triple net rent expense of USD 210.0 million to cash interest, Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 722.8 million covers the total 1.10x. The 2026 term loans cost at least USD 105.4 million a year even at the 3.0% floor plus the lower 6.5% base-rate margin, and more under the 7.5% Term SOFR margin, and part of the interest may be paid in kind [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 335.7 million over the last twelve months [CP-1 financials table].

Liquidity is the decisive issue. Cash of USD 390.2 million and reported revolver availability of USD 195.8 million total USD 586.0 million, compared with a six-month free cash outflow (operating cash flow less capital expenditures and capitalized software) of USD 359.1 million [CP-1 liquidity chart data; Q2 2026 10-Q page:5]. Revolver commitments are due to fall to about USD 319 million from October 2026 while USD 303.75 million is drawn, which leaves essentially no headroom once the reduction applies, before other usage of USD 19.75 million that CP-1 could not explain [Q2 2026 10-Q page:33]. Whether the reduction occurred, and how it was met, is Not supplied because the pack ends at August 14, 2026.

Covenant protection exists only through a conditional waiver. In May 2026 the required lenders conditionally waived the consolidated net leverage ratio covenant for each quarter from March 31, 2026 until the earlier of the company’s election or the day before the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2027, subject to minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver [Q2 2026 10-Q page:38]. The company states that it does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement or the reinstated covenant absent the financings under discussion, and that substantial doubt about going concern exists [Q2 2026 10-Q page:11]. The waiver level and the reported ratio are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable.

The structure divides the debt across two borrower groups. Parent-group debt is USD 2,898.3 million: USD 1,413.3 million of first lien revolver and 2026 term loans and USD 1,485.0 million of senior notes. Bally’s Intralot debt is USD 2,011.8 million, and Bally’s Intralot does not guarantee the parent’s debt [CP-1 debt table; CP-1A Transaction summary]. The two Intralot-linked segments produced USD 86.7 million of Q2 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDAR, leaving USD 37.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA from casinos, North America Interactive and corporate cost after rent [Q2 2026 10-Q page:48]. The mapping of segments to legal entities is not supplied, so parent-level leverage is only indicative; on this basis it is about 19.4x annualized Q2 2026 and 23.8x last twelve months.

Earnings quality is limited by add-backs and by margin pressure. Add-backs for transaction, development, merger, share-based and other items were USD 106.4 million in the six months to June 30, 2026, 43.0% of Adjusted EBITDA of USD 247.3 million [Q2 2026 10-Q page:48]. Q2 2026 revenue rose to USD 792.2 million while Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 124.0 million from USD 129.2 million, with gaming expenses at 52% of gaming revenue against 43% a year earlier [CP-1 segment base; CP-1A operating model].

Maturities are light until 2029 but the revolver and the 2029 wall matter. Debt maturing through 2027 is USD 141.4 million, 2028 is USD 282.3 million and 2029 is USD 1,007.0 million; the USD 1,109.5 million of 2026 term loans fall due in 2029 instead of 2031 if the 2029 Notes are still outstanding then, which would lift the 2029 amount to USD 2,116.5 million [CP-1 maturities chart data]. Refinancing of the 2029 Notes is therefore linked to the secured term loan maturity.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength, Documentary Fact: a diversified, licensed operating base. The company runs 19 US land-based casinos, a large online gaming business and a lottery technology business, with no customer above 10% of revenue, and holds Rhode Island master contracts to 2043, a New York gaming license and a Chicago development [CP-1A Company and operating model; Company profile]. This supports revenue durability, although segment cash earnings are not evenly distributed.

Strength, Documentary Fact: lender engagement and external funding for part of the capital programme. Lenders granted a waiver and amended the revolver in 2026, and GLPI has committed to advance up to USD 940.0 million for Chicago construction, which reduces the company’s own capital need there [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Lender engagement lowers near-term acceleration risk but does not remove the conditions.

Strength, Documentary Fact: contained near-term amortisation. Remaining 2026 and 2027 maturities total USD 141.4 million, and a parent revolver default has no implications under Bally’s Intralot’s debt documents [CP-1 maturities chart data; Q2 2026 10-Q page:11]. This limits contagion from a parent-level default to the Intralot group.

Strength, Analyst Interpretation: real estate and asset monetisation capacity. The Bally’s Twin River sale-leaseback realised USD 700.0 million of consideration, and the company lists asset monetisation among its plans [CP-1A Transaction summary]. This is also a weakness because each sale adds fixed rent, so I count it only as a source of liquidity, not of lower fixed charges.

Weakness, Documentary Fact: leverage and cover. Gross leverage of 9.57x, net leverage of 8.81x and cover of 1.15x leave little cushion, and the fixed-charge cover including rent is 1.10x [CP-1 charts; calculations below].

Weakness, Documentary Fact: liquidity and going concern. Operating cash flow is negative, cash fell from USD 798.4 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 390.2 million at June 30, 2026, and the latest filing states substantial doubt [CP-1 liquidity chart data; CP-1A Company profile].

Weakness, Analyst Interpretation: structure and control. A controlling sponsor holds 67.1%, no equity support is documented, parent creditors rank behind Intralot creditors at the Intralot level, and 42.1% of Intralot equity belongs to others [CP-1A Company profile; Governance]. The sponsor’s response is the key unknown.

Weakness, Documentary Fact: reporting quality and regulation. The 10-K reports an adverse opinion on internal control because of a material weakness, results were first issued as preliminary, and the Rhode Island regulatory agreement restricts payments and debt incurrence above a 5.50 to 1.00 leverage trigger whose definition and status are not supplied [CP-1A Company profile].

Weakness, Documentary Fact: uncommitted large projects. The USD 4.0 billion Bally’s Bronx project has a non-binding loan term sheet and a letter of intent with a potential equity investor, and construction at Chicago continues [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Funding competes with debt service.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Weak and stressed fundamental credit: leverage of 9.57x, cover of 1.15x, negative operating cash flow and a going concern warning; near-term outcome depends on financing execution and the waiver | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, interest cover and liquidity chart data; CP-1A Company profile (going concern); Q2 2026 10-Q page:11 |

| Thesis: a diversified, licensed gaming business has been levered and expanded faster than its cash earnings, so creditors depend on refinancing, asset sales and sponsor action rather than on free cash flow | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 financials; CP-1A Transaction summary |

Confidence is Medium, not High, because CP-0 and CP-1A carry open High-severity gaps (no executed agreements, nothing after August 14, 2026, perimeter and cash split between the parent group and Bally’s Intralot not supplied) and CP-1 ratios are not like-for-like across dates.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Liquidity shortfall and waiver failure | Cash used in operations, project spend and the October 2026 revolver reduction run ahead of financing; the waiver depends on a minimum liquidity level that management does not project it will meet | Reinstated covenant, possible acceleration of the Credit Agreement and a going concern outcome | Critical | CP-1 liquidity; Q2 2026 10-Q page:11, page:38 |

| Interest and rent burden | Cash interest takes 86.7% of Adjusted EBITDA and rent adds more; the 2026 term loans cost at least 9.5% | Debt cannot be reduced from cash earnings; refinancing at similar cost would leave cover near current levels | Material | CP-1 interest cover; CP-1A Transaction summary |

| Structure and cash trapping | Intralot debt does not guarantee the parent, 42.1% of Intralot equity is minority-owned, and earnings outside the Intralot segments were about 30% of group Adjusted EBITDA in Q2 2026 | Parent creditors rely on distributions that may be restricted; parent leverage is above the group ratio | Material | CP-1 debt table; CP-1A Company profile |

| Earnings pressure | UK gaming tax increase, gaming cost ratio up to 52% of gaming revenue, and add-backs of 43.0% of six-month Adjusted EBITDA | Adjusted EBITDA may overstate recurring cash earnings | Material | CP-1A Company and operating model; Q2 2026 10-Q page:48 |

| Capital programme and sponsor behaviour | Bronx, Chicago and Las Vegas spending without committed funding; a controlling sponsor with no documented support | Capital calls compete with debt service; outcomes depend on one holder | Material | CP-1A Transaction summary and Governance |

| Regulatory and reporting | Rhode Island 5.50 to 1.00 trigger, adverse internal control opinion, preliminary results | Payment and incurrence limits may apply; reported figures carry control risk | Material | CP-1A Company profile |
## Calculations
All amounts USD. Inputs are from CP-1 or CP-1A unless a page is given.
- Cash interest share of Adjusted EBITDA: 444,640 / 512,810 = 86.7% (thousands).

- Fixed charge cover: Adjusted EBITDAR 722,846 / (cash interest 444,640 + rent expense 210,036 = 654,676) = 1.10x (thousands; CP-1 financials table). Rent is the expense line; cash rent paid in six months 2026 was 133,561 thousand (Q2 2026 release page:8).

- Liquidity: cash 390.2 + reported revolver availability 195.8 = 586.0 (USD million). Six-month free cash flow: (265,936) − 73,954 − 19,227 = (359,117) thousand, so an outflow of 359.1; ratio 359.1 / 586.0 = 61.3%. This excludes the license fee of 502.0 and the contingent payment of 115.0 paid in the period, and the sale-leaseback proceeds of 685.0 (Q2 2026 10-Q page:5).

- Revolver after the October 2026 reduction: commitments about 319 less drawn 303.75 = 15.25; less unexplained usage of 19.75 = (4.5). This is arithmetic on stated amounts, not a reported figure; drawings may have changed.

- 2026 term loan minimum cost: base-rate option 3.0% floor + 6.5% margin = 9.5%; 1,109.518 × 9.5% = 105.4 per year; Term SOFR option 3.0% + 7.5% = 10.5%, or 116.5 per year. Both are floors before any PIK election; the rate in effect is not in the pack (Q2 2026 10-Q page:34).
- 2029 maturities with springing date: 1,006.996 + 1,109.518 = 2,116.514 (CP-1 maturity chart; Q2 2026 10-Q page:32 footnote 1).
- Segments: Intralot-linked B2B 21,931 + B2C 64,739 = 86,670 (thousands) of Q2 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDAR 187,515 (46.2%). Remainder of Adjusted EBITDA: 124,034 − 86,670 = 37,364.

- Indicative parent-level leverage: 2,898.268 / (37.364 × 4 = 149.456) = 19.4x. Last twelve months: Intralot-linked segments 361,497 (FY2025 B2B 38,489 plus B2C 323,008) + 188,878 (six months 2026) − 159,340 (six months 2025) = 391,035; remainder 512,810 − 391,035 = 121,775; 2,898.268 / 121.775 = 23.8x. Limits: segments are not legal entities, B2B includes the company’s licensing business, B2C includes a UK casino, corporate costs are not allocated by entity, and minority interests are ignored. Indicative only; Analyst Interpretation.

- First lien sensitivity (not a covenant test): first lien debt 303.750 + 1,109.518 = 1,413.268; net of consolidated cash 390.184 = 1,023.084; over consolidated LTM Adjusted EBITDA 512.810 = 2.0x; over the remainder excluding Intralot-linked segments 121.775 = 8.4x. The revolver test is 4.00 to 1.00 when utilization exceeds 25% (Q2 2026 10-Q page:65); the result swings across it depending on the EBITDA perimeter, which is why the covenant definition is a High gap.

- Add-backs, six months to June 30, 2026: transaction costs 28,568 + development costs 33,264 + share-based compensation 4,356 + merger and Intralot costs 10,953 + other 29,298 = 106,439; 106,439 / 247,318 = 43.0%. Q2 2026: 21,343 + 20,306 + 1,805 + 2,195 + 20,715 = 66,364; 66,364 / 124,034 = 53.5% (Q2 2026 10-Q page:48). The sale-leaseback gain of 105,845 is excluded from Adjusted EBITDA.

| Nothing after August 14, 2026, including the October 2026 revolver reduction, Fifth Amendment terms, Bronx loan, equity sale and evoke financing | The central question is whether financing closed | Credit view | High | Supply later 8-Ks and the Q3 2026 report if filed by the cutoff |

| Parent group versus Bally’s Intralot cash, earnings and intercompany restrictions; guarantor list | Parent leverage and access to Intralot cash cannot be measured | Structure risk | High | Supply guarantor schedules and entity-level accounts |
| Rhode Island regulatory leverage definition and status | Payments and incurrence may be restricted | Regulatory risk | Medium | Supply the agreement or certificate |
| Last-twelve-month ratios mix Successor and Predecessor periods and a changing perimeter | Trend in leverage is indicative | Leverage | Medium | Obtain pro forma figures |
| Sponsor intentions and any equity commitment | Decisive for outcome | Credit view | High | Supply sponsor statements or the proxy |
| Market prices, ratings and peer data | Not required for fundamental view; no relative value is given | None | Low | Keep Not supplied |
## Next module

- CP-5 should verify each cited locator and calculation in this answer, especially the borrower-group split, the indicative parent leverage, the first lien sensitivity and the add-back sums, and should carry the High gaps above as restrictions on any use of the credit view.
